## Observed Facts

- **Count:** 20,217 BGL Log Entries contain "ciod" (case-insensitive substring on the message). The scope is BGL, 2005-06-01 to 2005-07-01 (end exclusive), with no component or level filter [E1]. These are Log Entries, not incidents.
- **First match:** line 4988, 2005-06-03 16:17:40.190, node R26-M0-NC-I:J18-U11, component APP, level FATAL [E1]. The message is `ciod: Error loading /p/gb2/stella/RAPTOR/65641/raptor: invalid or missing program image, No such file or directory`.
- **Just before (lines 4980–4987) [E2]:**
  - Lines 4980–4983 (16:12:35–36) are KERNEL INFO correctable-error lines on node R16-M1-N2-C:J17-U01. They read "CE sym 2, ..." and "total of 31 ddr error(s) detected and corrected".
  - Lines 4984–4987 (16:16:26) are KERNEL INFO "generating core.N" lines, on nodes R22-M0-NB, N9, NF and NF. N is 257, 385, 65 and 1.
  - These come from different racks (R16 and R22) than the first ciod error (R26).
- **Just after (lines 4989–4996) [E2]:**
  - Eight more identical APP FATAL "Error loading ... raptor" lines follow within about 0.26 s (16:17:40.23 to 16:17:40.45). They come from other nodes in R26-M0 (NC, N8, N4, N0) and R27-M1-NC. Each node appears with both the U11 and U01 units.

## Hypotheses

- The failure looks like a job launch problem. The executable `/p/gb2/stella/RAPTOR/65641/raptor` was missing or unreadable when ciod tried to load it. Possible reasons are a bad path, a filesystem or mount problem, or a job that was cleaned up or never staged. The same message arriving from many nodes in milliseconds fits one job being loaded across many nodes.
- The core dumps and correctable memory errors a few minutes earlier are probably unrelated. They are on different racks, and nothing in the text links them to the load failure. A previous job crashing on those nodes is possible, but I can't show it.

## Unknowns

- I only inspected the first 5 matches and the 17 lines around the first one. I don't know whether the other ~20,200 entries share this message or include other ciod failure types.
- The logs don't show the path's state on the filesystem. They also don't show which job or user launched it, or whether the "generating core" lines relate to it.
- A "ciod" substring match can include entries where ciod is only mentioned in passing.

## Next Step

Run `count_by` on BGL with query "ciod" over the same time range, grouped by `component` and `level`. Then run it again with query "Error loading" to see how much of the 20,217 is this one message. Use `trend` by hour or day to see whether it is a one-off burst or recurring. If the same raptor path repeats, check that file and the filesystem mount on the nodes involved.
